utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear my own words in B/C/S on Channel 4, which most likely was a small mistake. Good afternoon again to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are a few matters I would like to briefly raise. There seems to be a matter in relation to D239. I was informed that there might be a request to change the status from public into under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, there is. I apologise for the delay. This is part of a package of documents we've been asked to have under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same true for the Simatovic Defence? Then D239, the status, will be changed into admitted under seal. There were numbers still to be assigned to certain documents. The one is a witness statement, 1D4851. Madam Registrar, that would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D258 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D258 is admitted under seal. Same is true for diagrams created by a witness and attached to the statement 1D2589, would receive number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be D259 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted under seal. Yes. Defence document 1D4852 is MFI'd but it did not appear any earlier on the 65 ter exhibit list. May I take it that there are no objections against - because that should be the first step - it to be added to the 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No objection to the addition to the 65 ter list, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Same is true for the Simatovic Defence. Then formally this document, which was already MFI'd, is that leave it now granted to add it to the 65 ter list. Then we move into closed session in order to further hear the evidence of the present witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Groome, I think that everyone was still waiting for an e-mail message by Mr. Ignjatovic but at least I haven't seen anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Nor have I, Your Honour. Given his expression of wishing to inform the Chamber directly, I just assumed that he had done that and had not cc'd the Prosecution. I'm somewhat surprise that he has not. He was very clear that he would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least I'm not aware, but I'll further ask the Chamber staff I met an hour ago approximately, I'll further ask to update that information. But as long as we haven't received anything, it's clear that the Chamber intends to ask the Republic of Serbia to get further details for the request for protective measures. If we do not receive anything meanwhile spontaneously, then we'll proceed for the time being as we decided to do last Friday. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I just address you briefly before the witness comes in, please, on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On this issue. Yes, now before the witness comes in is not possible anymore because the witness is in. But my recollection was that he doesn't speak or understand English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Very, very basic but he may follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He may follow. So you would prefer to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I can -- I would request that the Court -- I also spoke to Mr. Ignjatovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- and he assured me he would communicate with the Chamber and he would communicate that their position was a request and not a demand and that the witnesses shouldn't be concerned about being prosecuted, and I would invite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You would very much like the witness to know that. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we'll then further verify -- yes, the witness may put on his earphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, Chamber staff and the Registry will verify whether anything can be found. I, nevertheless, intend to proceed. But I might say, but in more cautious terms, a few words about that, if that would work to for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness DST-032. First of all, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber was informed that the Republic of Serbia expressed that you would have -- that there would be no need to have any concerns for you for being prosecuted for giving testimony. Now, the only thing is that we receive this in writing as well as we expect and everyone is now searching in their e-mails and in the post-boxes where to find that message, but since the Chamber has no reason whatsoever not to trust the information which was provided by one of the parties to the Chamber, and on that basis we would like to proceed at this moment. Mr. Jordash, does this meet, more or less, your -- well, I couldn't say your concerns, but does this meet what you would like me to do at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed. Mr. Jordash will now continue his examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, DST-032. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and good afternoon to everyone else. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, I want to keep moving forward in relation to some documents. But before I do that, Your Honours should have received a list of documents to be admitted pursuant to 92 ter, and we would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We received the list, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We would seek to tender the exhibits as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me just -- the first two on the list we have dealt with already. These are not the associated exhibits, but the first two we find on our list are now D258 and D259 under seal. So, therefore, we now start with 1D32 and following, is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's correct. And 1D1407.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have numbered from 1D32 up to 1D37. These are six documents. We then have -- perhaps I first ask Ms. Marcus whether there are any objections against the first six, 1D32 up to and including 1D37?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On the 92 ter chart that we received last week, there was a column for origin. And with respect to 1D32, 33, 34, 35, 36, and 37, we were told that the relevant correspondence that resulted in the provision of those documents would be provided. We have -- to the best of my knowledge we haven't received any RFAs or any origins with respect to those documents and so we would reserve our position on authenticity until we see the correspondence for those, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. They'll be MFI'd. Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The RFAs have been sent to the Prosecution. 1D1520. But obviously they haven't looked at them yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We MFI them for the time being. And, Ms. Marcus, could we hear from you by tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the first six documents on the list would receive numbers ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we need to have them under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D260 up to and including D265 are admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, just one question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I say "admitted," are MFI'd under seal. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can I ask why they're admitted under seal? Is it because we anticipate a protective measures motion from the Government of Serbia or what? What's the reason for those documents being under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Precisely that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we will hear further submissions by the government anyhow on what should remain confidential and what should not and then we'll ... Okay so then I correct my mistake: D260 up to D265 are MFI'd under seal. Next one, 1D364. Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, need to be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please, for the same reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the Simatovic Defence, apparently no objections. Then this document receives number D266, admitted under seal. Next one, 1D1276.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections by the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is an Official Gazette, does it need to be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's a confidential issue. Confidential Issue 18, 27th of July, 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't see that it is the Official Gazette as matters stand now. We have to consider confidentiality anyhow for all of these documents. This will be D267 admitted under seal. Then the next one, 1D1896, rule book.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal. No Simatovic objections. D268 under seal, with apologies to the Registrar that I've taken over part of her task. Then we have two documents which are already MFI'd, D233, D236. And the last one on the list is also already MFI'd, D151. And D233 is public. And the other two, D236 and D151, are under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I drew this diagram in Serbian. I designated the 18 centres, or, rather, I put 1 through 18. As for regular reporting, it was carried out by drafting, submitting, and forwarding original or primary material, or documents, in four identical copies. Two copies always remained in the centre, and you have them shown here. It was a copy for the operative who authored the document and another copy for operational archives. The same goes for the centre as would go for the 5th administration in the seat of the service. The other two copies which are marked here. And I may indicate them to you if you wish, in the small rectangle, we have one and the other. Upon a decision by the chief of centre, they were to be forwarded to the relevant administrations, either the 1st or the 3rd, and another copy was to go to the 5th administration. It wasn't necessary for the chief of centre to come up with the formal decision on the forwarding of these documents to the administrations in the seat of the service; rather, it was understood that it would be done once he signed cover letters for each of the administrations. Then documents would be put in separate envelopes and addressed to the relevant administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And would all information that was generated in the centres be sent to the 1st, 3rd, and 5th administration, or only certain information?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All information -- or, rather, primary documents or originals were not forwarded to all the administrations in the seat of the service. Some documents, as I mentioned in my statement, such as official notes which is used to document certain activities by operatives, as a rule were created in two copies which would both remain in the centre. Such official notes were not forwarded to the administrations in the seat of the service. The diagram has one precondition and that is that there are four identical copies of the document in question. We have it shown here. Two of those copies were to remain in the centre, whereas the other two copies were to be sent to two different administrations. In order to fulfill the conditions of this situation, it would have to mean that these documents had to be, say, associate reports, official notes of interviews, and reports on the application of certain measures. All those documents had to contain security-related information that was important for the work of service. That was the basic criterion by which the chief of the centre abided when making such decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Once the information arrived at the 1st and the 3rd administration, did all information get passed upwards or only certain information went upwards in the service?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once such documents were processed in terms of archiving and registering, they were immediately sent to the relevant chiefs of administrations. Those chiefs of administrations carry out a selection. In other words, they choose the documents that they will forward to the respective assistants of the chief of service depending on the line of work. It depended upon their assessment.

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Witness DST-032, I am inclined to become a bit nervous if an agenda, the same symbol, gets two explanations. Now, what I see is the legend, the original materials for 1 or 3 administration, is, as far as I can see, exactly the same as the 5th administration. I also do not know exactly what it means, original materials 1 or 3 administration. Is that coming from or addressed to? That is a bit unclear to me, because if I understand the diagram well, then the symbol presents the kind of information which is sent in the direction of the arrow between the various instances.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the last line of the legend you will see a circle next to which there is the explanation "analytical material." And if you look at the chief of the 5th administration and the link with the deputy and the chief, the materials that travel that way are analytical materials. Whereas the 1st and 3rd administrations, as operative and instruction administrations, in line with what you said, they forward to higher authorities original material or primary documents. These are documents which were created in the centres by operative workers authorised to collect information and compile material that in our terminology is called original material. And in the rule book on the work of the State Security Service from 1990, which was in force at the time, they are also called primary documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So if I understand you well, what your explanation is, is that the boxes with the diagonal cross in it, that the main thing we have to understand is that that is original material and that despite the legend but focusing on the diagram itself, that we can see that whatever original material is received by the 5th administration is not sent upwards, it is only the analytical material which is then sent further up in the system; whereas if original material is received by the 3rd administration or by the 1st administration, that they would send that material further up in the line but they would also receive that later back. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As you can see from this schematic, the 5th administration receives the material we spoke about, namely primary documents or original material. This is where that is. Analysed, assessed, and based on that, analytical material is produced which is then sent on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: question for you: We sometimes see lines with arrows but without any indication whatsoever of what kind of information is sent along those lines. I see three lines from the chief of service, direct lines, going down to the 1st, the 3rd, and the 5th administration, but it doesn't tell us what is transported or what is sent through these lines. Could you tell us what that is, or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the chief of service I see, for example, that original material goes up to him and is sent back to him. The same is true for analytical materials which is sent from the deputy up to the chief of service and then goes back again apparently once it has been processed, or. Now, I see lines from the chief of service directly to the box of the 1st administration, the 3rd administration, and the 5th administration. Now, what is -- what information is passed through those lines? Or what instructions or orders or whatever it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The chief of administration, for example, the 1st administration, can submit a document to the chief of service. And the chief, having acquainted himself with the document, returns it for some action to be taken in accordance with that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you say is that the chief of an administration can bypass the assistant chief of service and the deputy chief of service and directly address the chief of service, and then he could, in return, send back information to the chief of the administrations? What, therefore, is missing in the diagram is the arrow up from the 1st, the 3rd, and the 5th administration directly to the chief of service, because the arrow only points down and does not point upwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: such a way that it becomes illogic. But I do understand that the lines down from the 1st, the 3rd, and the 5th administration, without any indication of what kind of material is sent or what information is transported, that it should have arrows in both directions; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the interview in Belgrade, the Defence representatives showed me a figure for one year only, and that figure referred to countering extremism and terrorism, and I believe that figure was 8.902. Based on that, I stated in my statement that I couldn't imagine that the chief of service read more than a couple of documents a day, because the question, then, is what were the deputy, the assistants, the chiefs of administrations, special counsellors, et cetera, do?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can clearly be seen here. You're now asking me, and I'm answering, about how things were with the operative administrations, the 1st or the 3rd. At the same time, though, the same document that reached the chief of the 1st administration or the 3rd also reached the 5th administration. The 5th administration informs the chief of service in a synthetic way, not by means of individual documents. But, rather, based on the documents received by the 5th administration and that were processed there and turned into analytical material no matter what they were called at any point in time, the 5th administration informs the chief of service in a synthetic manner so that very few situations remain when the chiefs of the operative administrations can directly contact the chief of service. These situations are very infrequent because the chief of service is already acquainted by the 5th administration by means of the analytical material that has been created.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May we have, please, on the screen, P2979.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to deal very briefly with this because you may be asked about it by others, allegations in the Vreme newspaper relating to the year 2000. I think you referred to them when you attended court on Friday, allegations that you'd improperly destroyed documents. Would you like to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would. This copy of the Vreme magazine was shown to me by Defence. I refused to read the article. A few years back, and now I see it was in November 2004, this article appeared in the Serbian public and I didn't read it at the time either. Now I see that a group of senior officials -- first of all, I was never a senior official of the State Security Service. The only senior officials are the chief of the service and his deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Did I understand you well that you didn't read it at the time and when it was given to you by the Defence that you also refused to read it; is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. That is precisely what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, is it of any use to comment on something you haven't read.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness knows the substance of what he was accused of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's get rid of the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, there's one aspect of it that I would like to ask the witness about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then you put that to the witness. But I'm not much inclined for a witness who says I don't want to read it and to hear his comments on what he supposedly had not read. And I do not fully understand why you refused to read it if it is considered relevant by the Defence because it obstructs the way to get the best testimony. Mr. Jordash, could you please then -- let's not -- if you want to comment on allegations, fine, let's forget about the article. If there's any specific question Mr. Jordash would like to put to you in relation to this Vreme article, he will do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about one aspect which has been translated as follows: That you were responsible for destroying documents related to collaborators for special purposes insofar as the centres had these. Are you aware of the term "collaborators for special purposes"? Is that something that you've heard of before?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of this term of "collaborator" or "associate for special purposes." As far as I recall, there was something 20 years ago that was called "associates for particular purposes." As for these associates for special purposes, I encounter that term for the first time in 1991 when I was sent to the Kosovo SDB. There were dozens upon dozens of such files in different organisational units of the Kosovo SDB. I believe I need to provide an explanation to this Court. These people were associates --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you be quite brief because I've got some ground I need to cover, so please be brief.

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In briefest terms possible, these are associates for particular purposes who were engaged in cases of war or an immediate threat of war in the former SFRY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, may I invite you to have a look at the transcript. Page 34, first line, the sentence starting with "as for these associates," there seems to be a bit of an inconsistency. It may be a translation issue, and perhaps I also ask the specific attention from the interpreters. The witness told us that as far as he recalls 20 years ago there was called associates for particular purposes. And then he says: "As for these associates for special purposes," and that apparently is exactly the distinction he intends to make. So therefore could it be that when he said "as for these associates for particular purposes," rather than "special purposes," because I'm a bit confused. You see the point? He refers by a different name to what he mentioned before and he uses exactly the term where he says he's uncertain about.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please seek it to be clarified. Or if you can live with it, then we should move on. But it's unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: DST-032, what type of associates were you referring to in relation to the Kosovan DB? How would you term them?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about, as far as I remember, about associates for particular purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Have you ever come across the term "associates for special purposes" during your career in the DB?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Finally, do you admit or deny destroying documents in the way alleged by the Vreme article, i.e., improperly?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't only in the Vreme article, but also in different TV broadcasts that they referred to it. I claim in full responsibility that all documentation was destroyed in keeping with the rules of the State Security Service as of 1990. There is a problem, though, if I may explain, or actually two. First, this campaign in the media, the Vreme magazine and the TV, began in November when I was still special advisor of the BIA director.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: DST-032 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2004. I asked the then director to protect me from such allegations or such campaign. If he was unable to do that, I asked him to ask the government to step in because I acted under the then Law on the BIA Service, which decidedly states that the agency is duty-bound to assist his -- their employer if accused of something that is not substantiated. That assistance encompassed a number of different aspects and measures. In both cases my request was refused. The second problem was this: It wasn't only me, but any of us, we couldn't create a diagram like we did for you for the Serbian public to explain what it was that we did. We simply cannot do that because we are bound by the necessity to keep state and official secrets under the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you about a different subject, DST-032.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. For the parties, if possible, if we could finish the testimony of this witness after two and a half hours. You've had one hour now, Ms. Marcus. You would please try to do it as efficiently as possible, and then I don't know how many re-examination there will be, but, of course, let's try to see whether we would achieve to finish after the -- before the second break, which would mean that the next witness should be on standby, Mr. Jordash, the next witness who is scheduled for two and a half hours, which would mean that would take us well into Thursday. Could the parties consider and see whether there would be any opportunity that we would finish that witness perhaps on that Thursday. I am aware that we have a similar matter to deal with as we did with the present witness and the previous witness. Let's see how far we can come. I'm using cautious language which means that I'm not fully confident that we'll make it, but I also do not exclude for that possibility if everyone tries to focus on it. Mr. Jordash, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Only that I'd like to supplement the application for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's then do that tomorrow, or whether you set out in detail -- I do agree with you that there are three lines which we find in the application is not -- by quantity, is not overwhelming.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, the 29th of June, 9.00, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of June, 2011 at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: [Closed session] [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of the Chamber]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
